**Workshop performance: block** at `bf89eeda333da430b0d0272f8a6e745e65885c26`, solely on `docs/plans/221-seat-provenance/workshops/001-capability-bootstrap.md`. This is not a code, route-inventory or whole-PR verdict.

**P163-F001: correct the macOS ancestry/cache cost contract before choosing the design as written.** Option C's split is sound in principle, but lines 47, 57 and 60 prescribe C27 `ps` on ancestry misses, assert short-lived hooks/status lines are never tick-driven, and call repeated cached calls free. These do not establish the promised zero launches per tick per seat.

C27 concerns **argv verification during registration**, after in-process name/parent filtering; it does not require ps to learn a parent or start instant. Those kernel reads already exist on macOS in `crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:161-167,347-355` through libproc. The ordinary ProcLiveness wrapper can fall back to ps on an unanswered read, so merely choosing that wrapper would not establish a strict no-launch fast path either. B alone's claimed unavoidable per-tick ps cost is therefore not a valid reason to reject it; its other identity limitations remain for security/reviewer to grade.

**Required workshop correction:** specify in-process ancestry and process-start/lifetime checks for recurring requests on macOS/Linux, with an explicit no-launch refusal on unreadable evidence. Keep any necessary C27 argv launch confined to bounded bootstrap work at incarnation/adoption rate. State the bound on ancestry depth/work and how a fresh peer reaches a cached ancestor. A new short-lived PID does not already name that ancestor.

The cache needs an explicit lifetime mechanism, not just the phrase "per live ancestor": bind entries to ancestor pid+start and the registered incarnation; state how death, PID reuse, reparenting, tombstone/supersede or session change invalidates them, with bounded storage and lazy/event-driven retirement rather than a new per-seat poll. Rechecking current peer lineage/ancestor lifetime has a cost even on a hit. Do not claim it is free or rely on a generic lifetime PID cache.

**Budget to carry into phase 2:**

| Path | Cost shape |
|---|---|
| Long-lived token request | One SHA-256 of a fixed-size token, constant-time comparison and warm digest-to-incarnation map lookup; no launch. This is incremental authentication cost, not total route cost. |
| Short-lived cache hit | A constant number of peer-credential calls per connection, fresh lineage/lifetime checks as specified, and a cache lookup. Not zero work; no launch required. |
| Ancestry miss | O(D) bounded parent/start observations plus binding lookup; zero launches with the corrected strict kernel path. No whole-machine census. |
| Bootstrap/rotation | Nonce/token hashing, keyed single-use nonce consumption, digest persistence/map update, and any separately bounded verification; per incarnation, not per tick. |

No exact syscall count or latency is proved by this workshop. Token-map loading after a bounce and unused-nonce/cache expiry/capacity need lifecycle budgets before implementation. Rollout counters should be bounded aggregate metadata; measure interval deltas with positive route traffic, so zero "neither" on an unused route is not mistaken for migration proof.

**Prime-owned q-02–q-04:** bootstrap authenticity and the token mechanism can proceed without choosing them. Authentication must not implicitly decide inbound versus outbound restrictions (q-02), which prime is always reachable (q-03), or human/Telegram/system-message exemption (q-04). Treat the rollout's "still allowed" examples, particularly sidecar/system-message treatment, as identity classification only until those messaging policies are explicitly decided. All three remain open in public draft #112 at `a438316f839500f6e67a9364717f012ed7f7f005`; their printed defaults are not rulings.

The pinned workshop blob matches the reviewed file. Source/design analysis only: no CI, live benchmark, build, test or runtime probe was used as proof. Security/reviewer own F88 closure, bootstrap strength, TCP/Unix transition and the same-user residual. This block asks for a corrected workshop, not implementation work in this draft PR.
